stem:
The vaccine used to control tuberculosis (TB) is known as Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG). The vaccine contains live bacteria that have been selected so that they do not cause disease in humans.

Fig. 5.1 shows a macrophage that is in the process of engulfing the bacteria in the vaccine.

{{figure:figure_5_1.png}}

magnification $\times 4400$

Fig. 5.1

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Name the pathogen that causes TB.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how this pathogen is transmitted.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the events that occur in the body after the macrophage has engulfed the bacteria until the production of antibodies in response to the BCG vaccine.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Vaccines, such as BCG, stimulate the formation of memory cells.

Explain the role of memory cells in the body's defence against the TB pathogen.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Suggest why vaccination with BCG has not yet eradicated TB.
